text:
morgan: quick question — we need a tiny surface in the SDK/HTTP API so callers can hint routing preferences without breaking auth/quota. thinking headers: region, tier, and a small fallback policy. e.g.
```
X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1
X-Redwood-Tier: enterprise
X-Redwood-Fallback: prefer=low-latency; allow-fallback=true
X-Redwood-Debug: routing=1
```
We'd validate these server-side and ignore unsupported values. thoughts?

sanju: +1 on lightweight headers. couple of things: 1) keep header names short (x-rw-region, x-rw-tier) to avoid long proxies mangling them; 2) do NOT let tier header bypass quotas — must be used only for routing hints, auth/scopes determine actual tier privileges.

morgan: yep — exactly. the server should compute routing_decision = policy(token, hint, region_avail) and attach actual_decision to telemetry. UI can show requested_hint vs actual_route for each call.

tara: logging/telemetry concerns: we need an event that captures {requested_hint, applied_model_variant, fallback_reason, latency_bucket} so Optimize/Console can correlate cost regressions. also avoid logging customer-provided raw headers as plaintext (PII/security). normalize into enums before storing.

sanju: on the fallback semantics: we should model 3 modes: `strict` (fail if requested not available), `preferred` (try requested, fallback if necessary), and `aggressive` (prefer cheaper/quantized if capacity low). Example header: `X-RW-Fallback-Mode: preferred`. That is clearer than encoding multiple semicolon values.

morgan: good call. prefer `X-RW-Fallback-Mode: preferred|strict|aggressive`. And add `X-RW-Variant-Hint: nv512` for model variant preference (useful for quantized vs fp16). but default remains server-determined.

tara: one more: debug flags must be opt-in and only honored for internal tokens or via console toggles. we should have a `routing_debug` boolean in the response (not the full stack trace) and a `routing_id` to fetch detailed plan in the console for 30s.

router-bot: deploy-log: accepted routing header shape PR merged to staging (pr #4312). sample routing telemetry emitted:
```
{"routing_id":"rid_01G..","requested":{"region":"eu-west-1","tier":"enterprise","fallback":"preferred"},"applied":{"region":"us-east-1","model_variant":"gptx-q4_8","reason":"capacity-fallback"},"latency_ms":153}
```

sanju: security note — do not allow arbitrary region hints that map to other customers' private deployments. enforce region->customer mapping and deny if token not eligible for requested region. Also disallow `tier=enterprise` unless token's org membership indicates enterprise contract.

morgan: agreed. plan:
- accept short headers: `X-RW-Region`, `X-RW-Tier`, `X-RW-Fallback-Mode`, `X-RW-Variant-Hint`, `X-RW-Debug`
- server validates and strips raw header values, stores normalized enums in telemetry
- console: new per-request column `requested_vs_applied` + routing_id link to trace
- rollout: canary via deploy-bot to 10% of requests from internal orgs, then lift to beta orgs

deploy-bot: canary started (10% internal). watch `routing_id` trace for mismatches. ping @morgan @tara in ~30m. :rocket:

tara: tiny UX ask — when console shows fallback it should show cost delta estimate (applied vs requested) so customers can see when fallback saved money at quality cost. helpful for Optimize team.

morgan: love that. i'll add a telemetry field `estimated_cost_delta_tokens` to the event. ok i'll open the RFC with header names + validation rules and link to pr. closing thread for now, will ping when RFC ready.
